prompt: R parser #line directive placement constraint vs C
answer:
R is stricter than C:

- **R:** `#line` must begin as the **first five characters of the line**—no indentation or other characters may precede it. Whitespace may occur between `#line` and the line number or filename. Any remaining text on that line is treated as a comment and ignored.  
  — [R Language Definition, §10.5](https://rstudio.github.io/r-manuals/r-lang/Parser.html)

- **C:** The `#` must be the first preprocessing token, but it may be preceded by whitespace (and, after comment replacement, comments). Horizontal whitespace may also occur between `#` and `line`; for example, an indented `#line` is valid. Non-whitespace text after the directive is not generally ignored—it may cause an error or alter the directive’s meaning.  
  — [C preprocessing directives result](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62631133/what-characters-are-valid-to-occur-before-and-after-a-preprocessing-directive-in)

Thus, R requires effectively:

```text
#line 10
```

whereas C permits forms such as:

```text
    #line 10
# line 10
```
